newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia 1996 automotive sales slower - Govt.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia 1996 automotive sales slower - Govt.

text.p: Malaysian motor vehicle sales rose by 19.2 percent in the first seven months of 1996 compared with an increase of 68.7 percent in the same period of 1995, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.
The slower growth was due to sales of cars, which went up only 12.3 percent against a 73.3 percent rise in the first seven months of 1995, the ministry said in its annual Economic Report.
The report attributed the slower growth to Bank Negara's instruction last October lowering the margin of loan financing for cars to 75 percent, coupled with higher interest rates during the year.
However, sales of four-wheel drives and commercial vehicles increased 47.3 and 46.2 percent respectively, compared with increases of 54.5 and 51.2 during the same period of 1995.
